audited.claim: Megawatt charging takes a battery from 20% to 80% in 30–40 minutes, so it fits the driver's legal rest break
audited.note: Holds for one driver taking the mandatory break (C01, C03, C04); fails if the charger is occupied or the truck runs with a relay driver (C32)

audited.claim: Existing range already covers most long-haul work: 660 km covers 80% of missions, 90% with one 45-minute fast-charge break
audited.note: Company data from 70,000 connected tractors; not published, so it cannot be checked. Consistent with A01

audited.claim: Swapping needs rival truckmakers to share battery, hardware, software and protocols; Europe has no such standard
audited.note: No cross-maker swap standard is adopted in Europe; several OEMs take part in DIN SPEC work (C15)

audited.claim: Scania and partners target 1,700 high-performance charging points by 2027
audited.note: The target counts high-performance points across Europe without saying how many are megawatt-capable; Germany had 7 public MCS points at end-April 2026 (C26). The truckmakers' answer depends on this build-out

audited.claim: Swapping compresses a stop to roughly the time of a diesel refuel
audited.note: 5 minutes on CATL corridors (C07); Fraunhofer gives 5–10 minutes for automated European set-ups (C27)

audited.claim: Leasing the battery removes it from the truck's upfront cost
audited.note: True by construction; the battery's cost moves into a per-kWh or monthly fee that the station must recover (our model, C16)

audited.claim: Swapping costs more than standard charging but less than diesel
audited.note: Our German energy-cost-per-km check (C19): swap is cheaper than diesel at roughly 7 or more swaps a day at November 2026 diesel prices, about 13 at the 2025 average; it always costs more than depot charging

audited.claim: CATL runs more than 300 heavy-truck swap stations in China, serving 12 truckmakers and 16 models; plans 900 by end-2026
audited.note: 305 stations and the 900 target are in CATL's release; "12 truckmakers and 16 models" is Nikkei's figure — CATL's release says more than ten makers and over 30 models. 305 is one operator, not China's total (C06)

audited.claim: China shows swapping scales: swap networks are common where new-energy trucks reached 29% of sales
audited.note: Swap-capable trucks held a steady ~30% of electric heavy-truck sales in 2023–2025 (C20); one compiler shows 23% in Jan–Sep 2026 (C21). It scales alongside charging, it does not displace it

audited.claim: The Swaptopus venture (CATL and Octopus Energy) plans 30 European stations by 2035, first UK hubs in 2027
audited.note: An announced plan; entry signal for scenario S2
